guarantees.claim: Each bit b of data_o is combinational assigned to prng_key at the index given by RndCnstLfsrPerm[b].

assumptions.claim: RndCnstLfsrPerm[b] is a valid index into prng_key for all b in [0, Width-1]; i.e., 0 <= RndCnstLfsrPerm[b] < $bits(prng_key).
assumptions.cond: when the generate loop is elaborated
assumptions.risk: Out-of-bounds indexing into prng_key can cause X propagation or synthesis mismatch.

formal_sketch.antecedent: when the generate loop is elaborated

uncertain_points.claim: If parameter Width does not match the actual width of prng_key or the size of the RndCnstLfsrPerm table, out-of-bounds indexing can occur.
uncertain_points.cond: when the design is compiled with a given Width
uncertain_points.risk: Incorrect parameterization could lead to illegal reads of prng_key, causing X values on data_o or synthesis mismatch.

formal_sketch.antecedent: when the design is compiled with a given Width

uncertain_points.claim: The assign bit-permutes prng_key (likely a secret key) with a compile-time constant permutation RndCnstLfsrPerm. It is unclear whether this static permutation provides sufficient side-channel resistance or if additional masking is required.
uncertain_points.risk: If the permutation is fixed and known, an attacker may infer prng_key bits from power/EM side channels through data_o propagation.

formal_sketch.consequent: The assign bit-permutes prng_key (likely a secret key) with a compile-time constant permutation RndCnstLfsrPerm. It is unclear whether this static permutation provides sufficient side-channel resistance or if additional masking is required

security_implications: The assign reads prng_key, which is presumably a secret internal key used for masking, and outputs a bit-permuted version as data_o. If the permutation RndCnstLfsrPerm is static and known, this may leak key bits through power or EM side channels. Without additional randomness or masking, the direct mapping from key to output is a security concern.
